chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established brotherhood between me and Ali ibn Abi Talib, and married him to my daughter above His seven heavens, and made His closest angels witness to that, and made him my deputy and vicegerent. So Ali is from me and I am from him; one who loves him loves me, and one who hates him hates me. And indeed, the angels seek closeness to Allah through love for him.

key_terms.آخى: Established brotherhood (mu'akhat), referring to the divine pairing of the Prophet and Ali
key_terms.خليفة: Khalifah (vicegerent/successor), denoting Ali's authority after the Prophet
key_terms.مقربي ملائكته: The closest/nearest of His angels, the exalted angels who bear witness
key_terms.وصيا: Wasi (deputy/executor), a key Shia term for Ali's role as the Prophet's designated successor

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the brotherhood and status of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through Ibn Abbas, records the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declaring the unique bond Allah established between him and Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS). The Prophet enumerated several divinely-ordained honors: the brotherhood pact, the heavenly marriage to Fatimah (AS), the appointment as deputy and successor, the inseparability of their spiritual stations, and even the angels seeking nearness to God through loving Ali. This hadith was delivered in a public gathering context, affirming Ali's status before the Muslim community.
